# Kalasha Award for Best Lead Actress in a TV Drama

| holder_label = Most recent winner

The Kalasha Award for Best Lead Actress in a TV Drama is an annual acting honor presented by the Kenya Film Commission during the Kalasha International Film & TV Awards. It is dedicated to recognizing the female performer who has delivered the most compelling and artistically significant portrayal in a primary role within a television series.
The honor was inaugurated at the first-ever awards ceremony in 2009. Over the years, the category has tracked the evolution of Kenyan television, from early education-based dramas to modern high-production telenovelas and streaming originals.
The reigning titleholder is Sarah Hassan for her lead performance in Zari at the 13th edition ceremony held in 2024.
Criteria
Eligibility for this award requires an actress to play the leading role in a scripted drama series aired on Kenyan television or a recognized digital platform during the assessment cycle. The Kalasha Academy evaluates nominees based on their ability to carry the show's narrative, their technical acting proficiency and the emotional resonance of their character's journey.
The results are derived through a transparent, weighted voting system. The Kalasha Academy, composed of professional peers and industry experts, contributes 70% of the total score. The remaining 30% is decided by the general public, who vote via mobile and web platforms.

Ceremonies were not conducted in 2013, 2016, 2023 and 2025. Winners are listed chronologically.

Records
As of 2024, Sarah Hassan is the most successful actress in this category, having won twice for different television productions. She also shares the record for most nominations.
Most awards
* Sarah Hassan – 2 awards (2021, 2024)
Most nominations
* Sarah Hassan – 3 nominations (2021, 2022, 2024)
* Sanaipei Tande – 2 nominations (2021, 2022)
* Nice Githinji – 2 nominations (2011, 2017)
* Aisha Mwajumlah – 2 nominations (2021, 2022)
